Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can overfit a small validation set; selection bias can rival reported algorithm improvements ([Cawley & Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Sampled recommendation metrics can also reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation ([Krichene & Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Retain the pinned 99-negative protocol and describe results specifically as sampled HR@10. Fixed users and candidates support paired comparisons but do not eliminate validation-selection bias.

Suggested budgeted design, rather than a literature-prescribed optimum: preregister at most eight configurations including baseline, each covering all four categories; evaluate synchronized checkpoints every 40 epochs through epoch 200, giving at most 40 selection opportunities. Use preprocessing seed 0 and training/evaluation seed 42. Select solely by four-category macro validation HR@10, with a deterministic tie rule. Enforce the shared 43,200 GPU-second ceiling across training, failed runs, debugging and diagnostics; reduce trial count if measured costs require it. Report every configuration’s category scores, macro score, selected epoch and GPU time. Cap diagnosis at baseline plus two predefined contenders, one pass each; retain the prescribed 20-user full-catalog recommendation exercise as diagnostic evidence only.

For uncertainty, retain each user’s binary hit indicator. Bootstrap paired contender–baseline differences by resampling the same user indices for both models within each category, then average the four category differences; report 95% percentile intervals from 10,000 CPU resamples alongside category intervals. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals characterize user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models; they do not correct adaptive selection bias or measure training-seed variability. Keep hidden-test evaluation separate and final.
